title: SLO-driven retry orchestrator and idempotency adaptor migration plan
creator: Aisha Khan
description: We will build a centralized Retry Orchestrator that drives retry, timeout, backoff, hedging and load-shedding decisions from SLO targets and region-aware capacity signals. Paired with an Idempotency Adaptor that standardizes idempotency key propagation and conflict resolution across services and SDKs, this effort reduces duplicate processing across hedged requests and enables safer client-side retries.
background: Current implementations of retry, backoff, and hedged fan-out live in multiple services and SDKs. Teams have divergent defaults for timeouts, exponential backoffs, and idempotency semantics. In multi-region failover scenarios we've observed both cascading retries that exacerbate overload and silent duplication due to missing idempotency keys. This causes SLO blips, increased cost, and operational overhead during incidents.
goals: 1) Implement a centralized Retry Orchestrator library with SLO-driven policies exposed via config and control-plane. 2) Introduce an Idempotency Adaptor in SDKs and services to propagate canonical idempotency keys and handle deduplication/at-least-once semantics. 3) Migrate 6 high-traffic services and two official SDKs to the new patterns within the quarter. 4) Reduce retry-related P99 latency spikes during region failover by 30% and reduce duplicated downstream writes by 90% in hedging cases.
scope: Includes runtime client libraries (Node/Python/Go), server middleware hooks for request fingerprints, control-plane config, metrics/traces for policy decisions, and a documented migration path. Excludes: rewriting existing persistence-layer compaction or global cross-service transactions.
non_goals: Implement global distributed transactions or change downstream database schemas. This project will not alter billing semantics for retries; duplicate billing edge cases to be tracked separately.
proposed_design: - Retry Orchestrator: a small runtime module that evaluates SLO budget, recent error surge, circuit-breaker state, and region latency/cost signals to output: allow/deny retry, retry-window, backoff-factor, and hedging fanout count. - Policy Config: control-plane object (json/yaml) per-service with SLO targets, preferred-region list, and escalation rules. - Idempotency Adaptor: SDK abstraction to generate stable idempotency keys (UUIDv7-based + request-fingerprint), attach to wire format, and expose a canonical server-side header/metadata hook for middleware to deduplicate requests. - Server middleware: consult idempotency metadata and query a short-lived dedupe store (bounded TTL) before executing side-effecting operations.
api_changes: - New request header: X-Redwood-Idempotency-Key (string). - Retry Orchestrator API: orchestrator.decide(requestContext) -> {allowed: boolean, hedged: integer, backoff_ms: integer, reason: string}. - Control plane: /policies/{service} endpoints for rollout of changes.
sdk_impact: SDKs must: generate and surface idempotency keys by default for write-like calls; call the orchestrator.decide hook before retrying; support hedged request helpers that multiplex requests to multiple regions when configured. Backwards compatibility: if SDK consumer supplies their own idempotency key, honor it.
migration_steps: 1) Implement orchestrator prototype in runtime-lib and unit tests.
2) Implement Idempotency Adaptor in Node SDK and publish beta.
3) Integrate server-side middleware in 2 low-risk services for canary (read-repair style endpoints).
4) Run internal traffic split 5% with orchestrator enabled, collect metrics (duplication_rate, retry_rate, p99_latency, error_budget_consumption).
5) Iterate on policy defaults and add circuit-breaker thresholds for each service.
6) Expand migration to remaining services and SDKs; deprecate per-service retry knobs once stable.
7) Post-migration: remove legacy retry code paths after a 4-week stability window.
rollout_plan: Stage 1 (2 weeks): prototype + Node SDK beta. Stage 2 (3 weeks): canary in two internal services (non-critical traffic) with 5-25% traffic ramps. Stage 3 (4 weeks): extend to 6 services and Python SDK; enforce idempotency header generation in SDK defaults. Stage 4 (2 weeks): full production rollout with monitoring gates. Emergency rollback: control-plane policy toggle to disable orchestration per-service.
testing_plan: Unit tests for orchestrator decision matrix, integration tests with middleware and dedupe store, chaos tests simulating multi-region failover (fail region A, ensure hedging and dedupe prevent duplicate side-effects), canary dashboards and synthetic traffic tests to validate SLO behavior under load.
monitoring_and_slos: New metrics: orchestrator.retry_decisions_total{result=allow|deny}, orchestrator.hedges_total, idempotency.duplicate_detected_total, dedupe_store.hit_ratio, retry_latency_histogram. SLOs we enforce: client-visible p99 latency for text-generation endpoints unchanged within 10% during rollout; error budget burn for retries must not exceed historical baseline + 5% during canary. Dashboards: per-service policy decisions, region failover heatmap, duplicated-write alerts.
success_criteria: 1) Demonstrable 30% reduction in P99 latency spikes caused by retry storms during multi-region failover under synthetic tests. 2) >90% drop in duplicate downstream side-effects in hedged scenarios in production canaries. 3) SDK adoption: Node+Python default idempotency headers enabled for 95% of traffic to migrated clients.
risks_and_mitigations: - Risk: Missing idempotency integration in legacy services causing duplicates. Mitigation: feature-flagged rollout and strict canary phases; default deny hedging for services without dedupe middleware. - Risk: Orchestrator misconfig causing higher client latency. Mitigation: conservative defaults (deny hedging unless SLO slack present), rapid rollback toggle via control-plane. - Risk: Dedupe store adds latency. Mitigation: use in-memory bounded cache with async fallback; instrument latency and fail-open on cache errors.
